paragraphs.text: The Rav opens by explaining that each Shabbos receives its influences through the parsha read on it, and Haazinu falls between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur because it includes everything. Every Jew has his place in the Torah, and so too in Haazinu. He tells how the Ramban showed a student his own name hinted there, and notes that the mitzvah of writing a whole Sefer Torah is learned from 'write for yourselves this song', proof that Haazinu contains the whole Torah.

blocks.heading: The Ramban: a promise with no condition

paragraphs.text: The Rav brings the Ramban on Devarim 32:40: Haazinu sets no condition of teshuvah. It foretells the suffering and then the vengeance and redemption, so that the nations will not say the world is not run by Hashem. Citing the Sifri on the greatness of this song, the Ramban adds that even if a stargazer had written it one would have to believe it, since all its words have come true.

blocks.heading: Rosh Hashanah, the head of the year

paragraphs.text: From 'He tells the end from the beginning' (Yeshayahu 46:10) the Rav explains that Haazinu is read now because it parallels Rosh Hashanah. Just as the first letter of a word already holds the whole word in potential, Rosh Hashanah holds the whole year, which is a complete cycle. Therefore not one minute of its forty-eight hours may be lost: everything that will happen in the year is contained in it.

He adds that the past year was full of great events, and had we known them in advance we would have davened differently. To show that the redemption is near he tells how R' Nosson Wachtfogel, asked why the redemption he promised had not come, answered with a mashal: once the wedding has begun and the kallah is waiting, no one needs to push the chassan. Since the Aseres Yemei Teshuvah correspond to the ten utterances of creation, it fits that Haazinu, which contains everything, is read now.

Bachurim had asked the Rav the old question: why did thousands of Jews let themselves be led into the gas chambers without resisting? One who does not learn that Haazinu contains everything, he says, has a strong question. But Haazinu asks it first: 'how could one chase a thousand', and answers, 'unless their Rock sold them' (Devarim 32:30). Hashem handed them over; that is the only answer.

The same song promises vengeance for the spilled blood and says 'the day of their calamity is near' (Devarim 32:35), so it will not take long. When the nations ask where their G-d is, Hashem answers 'see now that I, I am He' (Devarim 32:39), meaning He will help.

blocks.heading: A tradition: no peace before Moshiach

paragraphs.text: The Rav describes a manuscript he holds of traditions from chassidic gedolim, each recorded with the name of the person it was heard from, as the Russian chassidim insisted. One tradition says that before Moshiach every nation will want to rule the whole world, as he sees between America and Russia. Another, in the name of the Apter Rav, says the nations will see that war does not help and will want peace, but will be dragged back and not allowed to make it. He applies this to the recent peace hopes around Egypt and Nasser: there will be no peace until Moshiach.

blocks.heading: Miracles of our days and the true redemption

paragraphs.text: The verses 'I will make My arrows drunk with blood' (Devarim 32:42) describe what will happen before Moshiach, when Hashem avenges the spilled Jewish blood. The Rav laments that we are too small to grasp the great miracles of our days. He sees a blessing of Bechukosai fulfilled when the enemies turned on one another and not one Jew was harmed, and reads 'a wild man' (Bereishis 16:12) as their nature.

He brings the Rizhiner that the redemption will come through nature. Yet the present government in Eretz Yisrael is not what Jews wait for: Moshiach is as the Rambam describes him, transforming the whole world, and anything else is a cheap imitation, though it may be a preparation.

blocks.heading: Why Haazinu is called a song

paragraphs.text: The Rav asks why Haazinu is called a song, when apart from its last verses it tells of bitter things. He answers with the Sfas Emes on why Rosh Hashanah speaks so much of judgment: Jews love Hashem so much that they want to be judged by Him, like a child who runs to his mother though she may slap him, because with her it is safer than outside. It is a great merit that Hashem remembers us, which is why the day is called Yom HaZikaron.

blocks.heading: Emunah turns the decree into song

paragraphs.text: As the Ramban teaches, Haazinu teaches emunah, and saying it daily is a segulah for emunah. Since every Jew's life is written there, nothing is chance: what comes may be bitter but not bad, like a bitter but excellent wine. Not the White House or the Kremlin decides destiny; 'He who sits in heaven laughs' (Tehillim 2:4). Therefore Haazinu is a song of joy.

blocks.heading: The shofar and its hundred sounds

paragraphs.text: The Rav brings a responsum of the Rambam: standing on the bimah with the shofar, he remembered Who commanded it and trembled. The shofar is Hashem's message, and its hundred sounds match the ten utterances of creation, each including ten, with the first tekiah before them all. Haazinu holds the whole year's course, so even its harsh closing verses, unlike other sidros, are a song when one knows they come from Hashem.

blocks.heading: Davening with emunah and answering amen

paragraphs.text: The success of the Aseres Yemei Teshuvah, the Rav says, is davening well, and that depends on emunah: as if one saw the Judge writing the year's decree. Haazinu calls Jews 'children in whom there is no faith' (Devarim 32:20), which the Midrash reads as those who do not answer amen, and this brought the persecutions.

This explains why the Shulchan Aruch says of one who talks during chazaras hashatz that his sin is too great to bear, the words said of Kayin. R' Elchonon Wasserman noted that every minute of galus is pikuach nefesh, so one who does not answer amen prolongs it.

blocks.heading: Rosh Hashanah, the day of gathering

paragraphs.text: Chassidim went to great lengths to be with their Rebbe on Rosh Hashanah, because it is a day of gathering; 'yom teruah' (Bamidbar 29:1) is a day of friendship. Following Sefer Yetzirah's world, year and soul, all the days of the year gather to their head, as the blood rushes to the heart, and all souls gather to their root.

Had we merited, this would happen in place too, as in 'the lost ones will come… and bow on the holy mountain in Yerushalayim' (Yeshayahu 27:13). The shofar is the signal, like a shepherd's horn calling his flock, summoning all to their root, Hashem.

blocks.heading: The point of yechidah and Malchiyos

paragraphs.text: In galus, the Rav says, each Jew must find the holy mountain within: the point of yechidah, where all Jewish souls are one with Hashem; reaching it is the avodah until Yom Kippur. Malchiyos opens with Aleinu, which Yehoshua said breaking the walls of Yericho, because one must break the wall in one's heart. He tells of a Lechovitcher chassid lost in a forest on Rosh Hashanah, strengthened by remembering his Rebbe's 'HaMelech'.
A Jew who makes Hashem King over all his thoughts and deeds is the switch for the whole world. So 'lift up your heads, O gates' (Tehillim 24:7): let one's heart open for the King of glory.

From a letter about a tzaddik's words when hostages were taken, the Rav brings Rebbi, who sent back a calf fleeing slaughter and suffered thirteen years (Bava Metzia 85a). Why did Yom Kippur not atone? It was not sin but reality: as a person shows mercy, Hashem shows him mercy. So one must have mercy on Jews in danger.

blocks.heading: A call to daven with mercy

paragraphs.text: In these days of judgment, the Rav urges, one must not forget for a minute to daven with mercy for Klal Yisrael and Eretz Yisrael: our mercy is the master key to every locked gate. He prays that Hashem fulfill the other blessing of Bechukosai, that five chase a hundred (Vayikra 26:8), so that Jews may sing not only over suffering.
